name: American River, South Fork
agency: El Dorado County Parks / BLM Mother Lode Field Office / California State Parks

camps.name: Miner's Creek lunch area
camps.desc: A BLM lunch and primitive camp area with restrooms.

camps.name: BLM lunch and camp area
camps.desc: A recommended lunch or primitive camp site with restrooms.

camps.name: Hastings Creek camps
camps.desc: Several lunch and camp sites with no facilities on BLM land, from Hastings Creek to mile 13.4.

camps.name: BLM camp area
camps.desc: A lunch and camp site with restrooms.

rapids.name: Meatgrinder
rapids.desc: The opening rapid below Chili Bar.

rapids.name: Triple Threat
rapids.desc: Miner's Creek, on the right, is a recommended lunch stop with restrooms.

rapids.name: Troublemaker
rapids.desc: The last major rapid of the Chili Bar run. Commercial photographers often stand along it.

rapids.name: Fowler's Rock
rapids.desc: The beginning of the Gorge. Bends left over a gravel bar, then right toward bedrock; the current runs left past the rock and slaloms through boulders.

rapids.name: Upper Haystack Canyon
rapids.desc: A narrow, scenic gorge with fun waves over a long distance.

rapids.name: Satan's Cesspool
rapids.desc: The most challenging section of the run. A long rapid bending left around a low rocky island; a sneak runs right and the standard route left. A cliff forces the current back right into a final chute with ledges at top right and left. Clean and deep below with a large catch pool.

rapids.name: Son of Satan's
rapids.desc: A short pool after Satan's. The current heads toward the right wall, but moving left is easy. Runs together with Satan's at high flows.

rapids.name: Scissors
rapids.desc: The river bends left above the drop, then narrows through the length of the rapid.

rapids.name: Lower Haystack Canyon
rapids.desc: A long canyon with mostly continuous waves.

rapids.name: Bouncing Rock
rapids.desc: On far river right, a steep drop over the rock and into a hole. Easy to avoid.

rapids.name: Pre-Op
rapids.desc: The river bends right and runs mostly north toward Hospital Bar.

rapids.name: Hospital Bar
rapids.desc: Past boulders and down a chute with the largest wave on the river.

rapids.name: Surprise
rapids.desc: Appears when the lake level is low. Class II rapids continue to mile 20.

rapids.name: Salmon Falls
rapids.desc: Read-and-run wave trains, chutes and boofs. Exposed when Folsom Lake is low.

hikes.name: Sutter's Mill site
hikes.desc: Where James Marshall discovered gold in 1848, in Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park. Historic buildings, a museum and interpretive programs.

hikes.name: Dave Moore Nature Area
hikes.desc: BLM public land on river right to mile 9.9.

hikes.name: Indian grinding holes
hikes.desc: Grinding holes atop a large boulder on river right. Lollipop Tree, marking the beginning of the Gorge, is visible here.

rules.d: One Coast Guard approved life jacket per person on board. Children under 12 must wear theirs while underway in vessels 26 feet or less. A Class III or V whitewater life jacket is advised.
Wear a wetsuit when flows are above 4,500 cfs or when air and water temperature combined is under 120 degrees.

Summer flows from Chili Bar Dam are usually 1,000 to 2,000 cfs. Boatable flows above 900 cfs usually run 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. Sunday through Friday and 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Saturday, through the first weekend of October.
Upstream utilities may release up to 3,600 cfs on midweek evenings. Flows can rise quickly.
Both runs are Class III below 6,000 cfs. Above that some rapids are Class IV and for advanced boaters only. Above 8,000 cfs demand the utmost respect.
Most riverside land is private. Public lands are the only acceptable stopping places. Signs mark where BLM land begins and ends.
Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park prohibits all take-outs. Put-ins are allowed at North Beach.
California campfire permits are required on BLM lands during fire season from May through October.

landmarks.name: Indian Creek
landmarks.desc: Enters on the left. The beginning of the Quiet Zone.

landmarks.name: Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
landmarks.desc: North Beach river access (fee) with picnic and restroom facilities. Take-outs are prohibited.

landmarks.name: Highway 49 Bridge access
landmarks.desc: River access. Parking under the bridge is prohibited.

landmarks.name: Henningsen-Lotus County Park
landmarks.desc: River access with parking, restrooms and a boat launch (fee).

landmarks.name: Greenwood Creek
landmarks.desc: Enters on river right. The end of the Quiet Zone. Free BLM put-in for the Gorge run.

landmarks.name: Gorilla Rock
landmarks.desc: Also called Convict Rock, on river left.

landmarks.name: Lollipop Tree
landmarks.desc: Marks the beginning of the Gorge.

landmarks.name: Folsom Lake maximum elevation
landmarks.desc: The high-water line of Folsom Lake.

landmarks.name: Salmon Falls Bridge
landmarks.desc: Take-out on the right bank upstream of the bridge. Parking fees are charged.

access.name: Camp Lotus
access.note: Common take-out and Gorge put-in area

permit.status: No permit · free annual boat tag

items.d: El Dorado County requires private boaters to display a free annual registration tag on the boat, available at access-point information boards, local campgrounds and stores.
Non-commercial groups of 18 or more must register before launching, online or at the major access points.
From half a mile above Troublemaker (mile 4.4) to Greenwood Creek (mile 11.5), reduce noise near homes.
Every boat must carry a waterproof trash bag.
Use designated restrooms or carry a portable toilet if you use land without facilities.
